$comment: The public surface, classified. Read by scripts/verify-api-stability.mjs, which fails when a
barrel re-exports from a module listed in neither tier — so a new module cannot enter the API
without someone deciding what it promises. A new export inside an already-classified module
inherits that module's tier, which is the right default: adding `getRectArea` to geometry.ts
does not make it experimental.
stable: covered by semver. A breaking change to any of these is called out under a Changed or
Removed heading in CHANGELOG.md.
experimental: may change or be removed in any release. Each entry states which of three
reasons applies, and each reason is a fact about the repo rather than a feeling about the code:
- unobserved: shipped, typechecked, gated, never watched running.
- off-by-default: behind a policy prop no default configuration turns on.
- r3f-canary: reachable only through @infinite-canvas/react/scene, whose @react-three/fiber
peer range admits a v10 canary. The framework cannot promise stability across someone
else's canary.
Purity is NOT a stability reason and size is NOT a stability reason. scene-layer-geometry,
spatial-target, and window-proxy all sound like 3D and are all pure-core roots
(verify-pure-core.mjs proves it) with real consumers, so they are stable.
window-scene-shell and scene-model were both public and both dead on 2026-07-08, and were
unexported that day rather than classified. window-scene-shell exported fifteen names nothing
called; scene-model was a two-line re-export of window-proxy under pre-proxy names nothing
imported. An export nobody uses is not a feature waiting for a consumer, it is a promise
waiting to be broken — and the package has never been published, so unexporting cost nobody
anything. window-scene-shell.ts still exists on disk, since window-proxy calls one function
from it; it is re-exportable in a minor if a consumer ever wants it. That direction is cheap;
the other is not. This is why 'unconsumed' is not one of the reasons above: an unconsumed
export is not classified, it is removed.
typesExperimental: types.ts is a grab-bag — it holds InfiniteCanvasSceneLayer next to
InfiniteCanvasRect. Its experimental names are listed one by one and checked to still exist.

experimental.canvas-handle: unobserved — a debug and automation seam, not a consumer API. Its shape follows whatever drives it.
experimental.diagnostics: off-by-default — this policy exists to switch on the frustum probe layer, and nothing switches it on.
experimental.minimap: unobserved — landed 2026-07-08. No minimap has been drawn in a browser.
experimental.offscreen: unobserved — landed 2026-07-08. No arrow has been drawn in a browser.
experimental.rasterization-layer: off-by-default — the policy, scheduler, and snapshot capture ship behind the rasterization prop. P7 intends to rebuild the capture lane on html-in-canvas.
experimental.visibility: off-by-default — reads the store only the frustum probe layer writes, so every reading is null unless /scene is mounted with diagnostics.frustum.
experimental.scene-surface: r3f-canary — the surface contract the /scene entry implements.
